pages.text: "No peas! No spinach!" At the kitchen table, Pipo pushed peas and spinach to the edge of his plate. He ate only bread and cheese. Mom looked at the plate and worried.
"Tomorrow I will race the sheep to the hilltop!" Pipo took another bite of bread. "Then eat peas too." Mom nudged the plate closer. He turned his head away. The peas remained.
The next morning on the hill, Pipo's legs had no strength. Sheep were already leaping far ahead, but his legs felt too heavy to jump. "The sheep are there... why will my legs not climb?"
Grandpa Sheep climbed up with his stick. "Pipo, what do sheep eat to jump like that?" Pipo tilted his head. "Grass?" "Yes, only grass. Long ago, I ate grass and flew over these hills too."
Sheep grazed, then bounced to the hilltop. Only grass, yet so full of energy! "Wow..." Pipo tipped his head to look up.

Grandpa whispered, "Strength hides in grass. Peas and spinach are green like grass. A bite of green too! It puts strength in your legs!" Really? Pipo swallowed. A sheep beside him took another mouthful of grass.
At dinner, Pipo found courage. A bite of peas, crunch! "...Oh? Sweet!" He chewed spinach too. Not bitter—tasty! "A bite of green too!" Mom smiled beside him.
The next morning, how strange! His heavy legs felt light. Pipo leaped to the hilltop beside the sheep. Crouching there, both hands before his chest, he said, "My strength is back!"
That evening, Pipo offered his plate. "Mom, lots of peas, please! One, a green bite! Two, a bread bite! Three, bites of everything!" The plate soon became clean.
Mom hugged Pipo and kissed his cheek. "A green bite gave your legs strength, right?" Eating different foods brought growing strength. Pipo grinned. "A bite of green too!"
